scenarios.customerLine: Hi, I just checked my credit card statement and I was charged twice for my last capsule order. I only placed one order!
scenarios.repResponse: I'm sorry about that, let me check your account right away... I can see the duplicate charge from the 4th. I'm issuing a refund for the second charge now — you'll see it back on your card within 3 to 5 business days, and I'm sending you a confirmation email.
scenarios.intent: Routine billing correction. The rep has full authority to refund duplicate charges and resolved it in one exchange — no escalation signal present.

scenarios.customerLine: My machine's orange light keeps blinking and the coffee is coming out lukewarm. Is it broken?
scenarios.repResponse: Good news — that blinking light usually means the machine needs descaling, which also explains the temperature. I'll walk you through it now, it takes about 15 minutes, and I'm texting you a link to the step-by-step video as well.
scenarios.intent: Standard technical troubleshooting with a known fix. Customer is curious, not frustrated; the rep is guiding them to resolution.

scenarios.customerLine: My order was supposed to arrive Tuesday and it's Friday now. Where is it?
scenarios.repResponse: Let me track that for you... I see it was held up at the courier's regional hub. I've flagged it for priority delivery — it should reach you by tomorrow — and I've added a sleeve of capsules to your next order on us for the inconvenience.
scenarios.intent: Mild frustration over a late delivery, but the rep located the package, gave a concrete new ETA, and offered a goodwill gesture. Single complaint, de-escalating tone — within rep's scope.

scenarios.customerLine: I want to cancel my monthly subscription. I have too many capsules piling up at home.
scenarios.repResponse: I can take care of that for you. Before I do — if the issue is quantity, I can pause your deliveries for two months or switch you to a smaller box instead. Would either of those work better, or shall I go ahead and cancel?
scenarios.intent: Retention conversation, not a conflict. The customer has a practical reason, the rep is offering standard alternatives, and no manager request or repeated frustration has occurred.

scenarios.customerLine: This is the third time I'm calling about the same broken machine and nobody helps me. I want to speak to a manager. Did you hear me? I said I want a manager, NOW.
scenarios.repResponse: I completely understand, and I'm sorry it's taken three calls. I'm bringing my manager into the call right now — please stay on the line with me for just a moment.
scenarios.intent: Hard escalation rule: the customer explicitly demanded a manager twice in the same exchange, on a repeat issue (third call). The agent must initiate a warm transfer and brief the manager before connecting.
scenarios.managerBrief: Hi, quick brief before you join: the customer is Dana Cohen, calling for the third time about a milk frother that stopped working two weeks after purchase. Previous calls promised a replacement that never shipped. She has explicitly asked for a manager twice and is highly frustrated. Recommended opening: acknowledge the failed replacement, confirm a new unit ships today with express delivery, and offer a goodwill credit. She is a 4-year subscriber with high lifetime value.
